newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egypt state to sell up to 30 pct in miller.
newsitem.headline: Egypt state to sell up to 30 pct in miller.

text.p: Egypt's state-owned Holding Company for Rice and Flour Mills said on Monday it was offering investors up to 1.2 million shares or 30 percent of subsidiary Alexandria Flour Mills as part of the privatisation programme.
The holding company said it would sell an additional 400,000 shares or 10 percent of the mill to its workers, shrinking its stake in the company to 60 percent.
It said the shares would be sold at 75 pounds ($22) each and shareholders will be entitled to the five pound dividend for the financial year 1996/7, which ends on June 30.
The company and the agents for the sale, the National Bank of Egypt, did not say when the offer would open.
The sale comes as part of the goverment's privatisation-led economic reform programme, which is monitored by the International Monetary Fund and World Bank.
Flour mill stocks are among the most popular on the Cairo stock exchange but the state has said it will not give up its majority holding in the sector because of its "strategic nature."
